newsitem.title: ITALY: RESEARCH ALERT -- TIM upgraded by SBC Warburg.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT -- TIM upgraded by SBC Warburg.

text.p: Investment bank SBC Warburg said it had upgraded its estimates for the years 1996, 1997 and 1998 for Italian mobile phone group Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM).

The investment bank said in a statement that it was significantly upgrading its estimate for TIM based on strong subscriber growth at TIM in the fourth quarter of 1996 and the fact that TIM is a clear winner from the tax changes introduced with the budget approved in late December 1996.
It is upgrading its 1996 earnings per share estimate for TIM to 125 lire from 119 lire, its 1997 earnings to 214 lire from 160 lire, and for 1998 by over 50 percent to 292 lire from 193 lire.
SBC Warburg said it is therefore upgrading its price target to 5,500 lire from 4,000 lire, and rates TIM an outstanding buying opportunity at just 14.9 times 1998 earnings.

SBC Warburg said that the TIM card introduced in September 1996 had proved to be a runaway success, and TIM's main problem during Christmas was to supply enough cards to its outlets and frenzied customers. TIM managed to sell in excess of 500,000 cards in 1996, it added.

The investment bank said it is therefore upgrading its full year 1996 subscriber numbers for TIM to 5.7 million from 5.4 million previously and its market estimate to 6.4 million from 6.1 million. Its 1997 forecast for TIM is 7.5 million and 9.7 million for the market.
